# The simd Min and Max are the hardware instructions. On amd64 they return the
# second operand for a NaN and do not order -0 below +0, where Go's min and max
# (and math.Min and math.Max) propagate the NaN and order the zeros; arm64 matches
# Go. The result would depend on the machine, so float min and max are left alone.

cp ops.go ops.go.orig
loopvec -split .
! stdout .
! stderr .
! exists ops_simd.go
cmp ops.go ops.go.orig

-- go.mod --
module example.com/test

go 1.27.1
-- ops.go --
package test

import "math"

func Relu(dst, a []float32) {
	for i := range dst {
		dst[i] = max(a[i], 0)
	}
}

func Lower(dst, a, b []float64) {
	for i := range dst {
		dst[i] = math.Min(a[i], b[i])
	}
}
